rfi.description: France has ordered the expulsion of Xenia Fedorova, the former head of Russia Today France, accusing the Russian journalist of spreading Kremlin propaganda on French television and radio, including on channels owned by the Bolloré group, the Interior Ministry said on Wednesday.

rfi.description: South Africa is suffering a drop in its workforce, following the departure of thousands of foreign workers in the wake of a wave of xenophobic attacks, anti-migrant protests and intensified immigration enforcement.

rfi.title: Renault to face criminal trial in France over 'dieselgate' emissions scandal
rfi.description: Renault will face a criminal trial in France on aggravated fraud charges over accusations that devices in its diesel cars were designed to cheat clean air laws, the public prosecutor's office told French news agency AFP.

rfi.title: Rift deepens as US walks out of UN over French criticism of Trump
rfi.description: United States diplomats walked out of a United Nations Security Council meeting on Monday as their French counterparts were speaking, after Paris criticised the Trump administration’s human rights record and backed a second term for human rights chief Volker Turk. The move underlined the growing strain in relations between Washington and one of its closest European allies.

rfi.title: Family of missing French tourist demands Japan's national police take over case
rfi.description: A statue honouring Tiphaine Véron, the French tourist who vanished in Japan in 2018, was unveiled on Wednesday near the hotel where she was last seen. Eight years on and still without any solid leads, her family is now pushing for Japan's national police to take over the stalled investigation.

rfi.description: Uganda's health minister on Tuesday declared the country Ebola-free, following the latest outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic disease which infected 20 people and killed two in the country.

rfi.title: UK's Burnham pledges new drone tech to Ukraine in Zelensky meeting
rfi.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged new drone-jamming technology to Ukraine on Monday, using his first meeting with a foreign leader since taking office to underline Britain's continued military backing for Kyiv.

rfi.title: France and Spain race to contain wildfires before new heatwave

rfi.description: Iran's foreign ministry has said it had summoned the French ambassador to Tehran to protest the conduct of two diplomats, who were briefly detained earlier this month.

rfi.title: Senegal's Faye breaks ties with Sonko to launch new political party
rfi.description: Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye on Saturday launched a new political party called Kiiraay, following his high-profile falling-out with his former mentor and ex-prime minister, Ousmane Sonko, and his party Pastef.

rfi.title: Haiti schedules first elections in a decade for December
rfi.description: Haiti's electoral council just scheduled the first elections in a decade for December with a runoff in February. Earlier plans to hold the vote in August with a December runoff were postponed over security concerns.

rfi.title: Chad becomes fifth nation to quit ICC amid US pressure campaign
rfi.description: Chad has become the fifth country to begin a formal withdrawal process from the International Criminal Court in recent months, following Venezuela, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.

lemonde.description: Dans la région de Lanton, les bénévoles venus prêter main-forte sont exaspérés par les difficultés qu’ils rencontrent et par l’intransigeance des forces de l’ordre. Leur aide est pourtant précieuse aux yeux des pompiers.

lemonde.description: Cette nouvelle tranche est versée au titre du volet défense du programme de prêts de soutien à Kiev, destiné à financer l’acquisition de drones, de missiles, de systèmes de défense antiaérienne et d’avions de combat.

lemonde.title: L’Arabie saoudite est passée de la retenue à la riposte face à l’Iran et ses alliés
lemonde.description: Longtemps soucieux d’éviter un affrontement direct, Riyad assume désormais ses opérations militaires contre les réseaux soutenus par Téhéran. La multiplication des attaques contre ses infrastructures énergétiques et la fragilisation de ses voies d’exportation pourraient contraindre le royaume à s’engager davantage dans le conflit.

lemonde.title: Les associations engagées dans une course aux financements et aux économies pour pallier la baisse des aides publiques
lemonde.description: Les 1,5 million d’organisations non lucratives et leurs soutiens se démènent, tout en appelant à cesser les coupes budgétaires.

lemonde.description: « Quand bien même ils auraient été livrés, c’est du matériel grand public, livré dans l’urgence », dont « la robustesse » n’est pas suffisante, a réagi le représentant de la branche santé et action sociale de la CGT.

lemonde.title: Deux jours après le séisme au Japon, au moins 34 morts, des milliers de rescapés et des opérations de sauvetage sous la canicule
lemonde.description: Deux jours après le tremblement de terre de magnitude 7,1 qui a ravagé l’île de Kyushu, au sud de l’archipel japonais, des milliers de sinistrés privés d’électricité doivent désormais affronter des températures pouvant atteindre 38 °C.

lemonde.title: L’empereur Ashoka, un tyran sanguinaire devenu pilier de la sagesse
lemonde.description: « Quand gouvernent sages et philosophes » (3/5). Après la sanglante guerre du Kalinga, au IIIᵉ siècle avant notre ère, le jeune roi indien se métamorphose en défenseur du vivant.

lemonde.title: En Inde, la série « Delhi Crime » met en lumière le manque criant des moyens de la police et la corruption des responsables politiques
lemonde.description: « Tour du monde en séries » (4/6). Les viols et tortures infligées à Jyoti Singh, 23 ans, dans un bus de New Delhi en 2012 a traumatisé tout le pays. Ce crime barbare a aussi inspiré au créateur Richie Mehta une série qui s’attache à retracer le travail de la police pour retrouver les coupables.

lemonde.title: En Pologne, le parti ultraconservateur Droit et justice vole en éclats à un peu plus d’un an des élections législatives
lemonde.description: L’ancien premier ministre Mateusz Morawiecki a décidé de former son propre groupe parlementaire, emmenant 40 des 186 députés du PiS. Un coup dur pour la principale force d’opposition polonaise, menacée par un essor inédit de l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: L’écrivain belge Raoul Vaneigem, insurgé lyrique contre la société marchande, est mort
lemonde.description: Le philosophe, un des leaders du mouvement situationniste avec Guy Debord, prônait une liberté d’expression radicale. Dans son « Traité de savoir-vivre à l’usage des jeunes générations », en 1967, il règle ses comptes avec le capitalisme. Il resta, jusqu’à la fin de sa vie, un soutien attentif à toutes les alternatives autogestionnaires.

lemonde.title: Le rebond en trompe-l’œil de l’économie française au deuxième trimestre
lemonde.description: Après un recul de 0,1 % du PIB au cours des trois premiers mois de l’année, le léger rebond au deuxième trimestre (+ 0,2 %) est largement dû aux exportations, en partie dans l’aéronautique. L’industrie tient, tandis que les ménages demeurent prudents.

lemonde.title: Les dessous du projet de Gianni Infantino d’ouvrir la FIFA aux investisseurs privés
lemonde.description: La Fédération internationale de football a annoncé, mardi, son intention de créer une société commerciale, pour maximiser ses revenus, notamment de la Coupe du monde. Une évolution critiquée, notamment par l’UEFA, qui dénonce la « vente » du football.

lemonde.title: BTS ne participera pas aux Grammy Awards pour protester contre la nouvelle catégorie « pop asiatique »

lemonde.title: L’industrie en Europe n’est pas adaptée aux nouvelles crises climatiques
lemonde.description: Vagues de chaleur, inondations, incendies… L’adaptation au changement climatique n’est pas suffisamment prise en compte par les industriels dans leurs plans de financements et de fonctionnement, qui privilégient davantage la réduction des émissions de CO₂, selon une étude du cabinet Sia Partners.

Une nouvelle violation de l'espace aérien de l'Otan, qui suscite de nombreuses réactions en Europe.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : la validation de la loi référendaire relance le débat sur un 3e mandat

france24fr.title: Mégafeu en Gironde : les stigmates de l'incendie
france24fr.description:
Le mégafeu qui frappe la Gironde depuis huit jours a laissé sur sur son chemin destruction et impuissance. Quelques gouttes de pluie et des températures plus clémentes ont redonné espoirs aux pompiers : ils considèrent le feu "toujours stabilisé" mais restent prudents.

observador.title: Lucros da operadora de jogo MGM China descem 7,4%
observador.description: A MGM China declarou uma descida de 7,4% nos seus lucros, no 2º trimestre, justificando-se com uma quebra nas apostas em jogos de mesa VIP e mesas de jogo não-VIP nos seus casinos em Macau e Cotai.

observador.title: Governo cria linha de apoio a vítimas de tráfico humano
observador.description: A linha de apoio vai financiar projetos de prevenção e proteção de vítimas de tráfico humano, no valor de 100 mil euros. Governo destaca a importância de combater grave violação dos direitos humanos.

observador.title: Falta de ambulâncias do INEM leva a novo parto em casa
observador.description: O INEM foi chamado às 12h09 por causa de uma mulher grávida com "hemorragia e dores fortes" que acabou por dar à luz em casa e com a ajuda dos vizinhos. Só às 12h39 é que foi acionada uma ambulância.

observador.title: Seis das 12 salas de cinema do Nova Arcada em Braga reabrem
observador.description: As seis salas, atualmente em renovação, deverão abrir no último trimestre deste ano, após terem fechado em janeiro devido ao processo de insolvência da Cineplace, anterior empresa exploradora.

observador.title: PJ detém suspeito de abusar de crianças em Castro Verde
observador.description: Homem de 46 anos detido por suspeitas de abusos sexuais e maus-tratos da filha e enteada dentro da casa da família, onde vivia com as duas menores e a mulher.

observador.title: Chegámos ao fim da leitura? Ou nunca vamos deixar os livr...
observador.description: Partimos de um ensaio da revista The Atlantic para fazer as perguntas que interessam: a tecnologia tomou conta do nosso tempo? A literatura já não tem importância? Ou é tudo uma questão de perspetiva?

observador.title: 13h. Embarcação de recreio afunda-se no Tejo após incêndio
observador.description: Barco ardeu em frente a Algés, mas o único tripulante foi salvo. O comandante do Porto de Lisboa conta o que se passou ao Observador.

observador.title: Banco de Moçambique. Endividamento público afeta mercado
observador.description: O banco central volta a identificar o agravamento do risco fiscal como um dos principais fatores de incerteza para a economia moçambicana. O stock da dívida pública disparou 20% nos últimos 5 anos.

spiegel.title: Ebola in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo: Mehr als 1500 Tote gemeldet
spiegel.description: Das Ebolavirus breitet sich in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo so schnell aus wie nie zuvor. Bei vielen Betroffenen ist nicht klar, wo sie sich angesteckt haben.

spiegel.title: UEFA-Notfalltreffen wegen FIFA-Investorenplan: Wie groß ist Europas Einfluss?
spiegel.description: Der europäische Fußballverband Uefa widersetzt sich dem Milliardenplan von Gianni Infantino – der will WM-Anteile an Investoren verkaufen. Sogar ein Boykott der nächsten Weltmeisterschaft wird erwogen.

spiegel.title: Hamburger Sternbrücke muss Weitertransport unterbrechen
spiegel.description: Es ist Millimeterarbeit, die neue Sternbrücke durch Hamburgs Stadtteil Altona zu manövrieren. Jetzt wurde der Koloss vorerst gestoppt.

spiegel.title: Startklar-Newsletter: Wie werde ich weniger perfektionistisch?
spiegel.description: Wie man die eigenen Ansprüche herunterschraubt – für bessere Ergebnisse. Wie viel Fahrradkuriere verdienen. Und wie man eine »Sofa« wird. Die Texte der Woche zu Studium und Berufseinstieg.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: 147 Millionen Euro Gewinn
spiegel.description: Erstmals kann die Bahn nach Jahren der Krise wieder positive Zahlen vorlegen. Konzernchefin Palla hat die Zahlen nun erläutert und weitere Ziele skizziert.

spiegel.title: Premier League - Newcastle United: Mit Matthias Jaissle bekommt Nick Woltemade offenbar deutschen Trainer
spiegel.description: Neuer Coach für Nick Woltemade und Malick Thiaw: Nach übereinstimmenden Medienberichten übernimmt Matthias Jaissle Newcastle United. Er kommt aus Saudi-Arabien.

spiegel.title: Hitze in Deutschland: Mediator über Streit bei hohen Temperaturen
spiegel.description: Pöbeleien in der U-Bahn, Streit unter Nachbarn: Wenn es heiß ist, steigt die Aggression. Mediator Jörn Valldorf beschreibt, was hilft, und warum hohe Temperaturen allein nicht das Problem sind.

spiegel.title: Australien: Entliehenes Buch an Bibliothek zurückgegeben – 150 Jahre zu spät
spiegel.description: Die Mahngebühren müssten horrend sein: Ein Mann hat ein Buch in eine australische Bibliothek zurückgebracht, das seit rund 150 Jahren überfällig ist. Jetzt soll es niemand mehr ausleihen dürfen.

spiegel.title: Amazonien: Spuren uralter Zivilisation entdeckt
spiegel.description: Von wegen unberührter Regenwald: Archäologen sind in Südamerika auf die Überreste einer bisher unbekannten Kultur gestoßen. Millionen Menschen dürften vor etwa 2000 Jahren dort gelebt haben.

spiegel.title: Kinder von Hollywood-Ex-Traumpaar gemeinsam bei Premiere
spiegel.description: Ihre Eltern dominierten in den Neunzigerjahren die roten Teppiche, nun übernehmen die Kinder: Bei der Premiere ihrer neuen Serie sind der Sohn von Richard Gere und die Tochter von Cindy Crawford zusammen aufgetreten.

spiegel.title: Trotz Irankrieg: Deutsche Wirtschaft wächst minimal
spiegel.description: Die deutsche Wirtschaft trotzt den globalen Konflikten und Spannungen. Ökonomen werten die Zahlen als erfreuliches Signal. Sie seien aber weit entfernt von einem Befreiungsschlag.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Amal und George Clooney müssen ihr Haus evakuieren
spiegel.description: Familie Clooney ist seit fast fünf Jahren in Brignoles zu Hause. Nun musste sie ihr Bauernhaus wegen der Waldbrände verlassen. Dem Dorf und seinen Bewohnern wollen sie treu bleiben, »egal, was geschieht«.

spiegel.title: München: Mann fragt nach Fahndung nach sich und wird verhaftet
spiegel.description: Geht ein Mann in eine Polizeidienststelle und wird verhaftet: In München fragt ein 42-Jähriger, ob er möglicherweise gesucht werde. Als die Beamten seine Identität überprüfen, finden sie einen Haftbefehl.

spiegel.title: London: Ex-Manager erhält Millionen-Entschädigung für Stigmatisierung nach Elternzeit
spiegel.description: Goldman Sachs rühmt sich als Vorreiter beim Elternurlaub. Einem Manager, der diesen in Anspruch nahm, wurde kurz darauf gekündigt. Ein Londoner Gericht lässt die Bank nun teuer dafür bezahlen.

spiegel.title: Katy Perry: Pop-Sängerin bei Konzert in aufblasbarer Flasche gefangen
spiegel.description: Auf ihrer aktuellen Konzertreihe lässt sich Katy Perry von Fans auf ungewöhnliche Weise durch die Menge tragen. Bei einem Konzert in Malta lief das anders als geplant.

spiegel.title: Ankara in der Türkei: Bürgermeister und Ex-Schauspieler Erdal Beşikçioğlu festgenommen
spiegel.description: Die Justiz in der Türkei geht weiter gegen Mitglieder der CHP vor. Mehr als 50 Menschen sollen festgenommen worden sein. Darunter der ehemalige Schauspieler Erdal Beşikçioğlu.

spiegel.title: Amy Winehouse: Vater muss Freundinnen der Sängerin fast eine Million Pfund zahlen
spiegel.description: Zwei Freundinnen von Amy Winehouse verkauften persönliche Dinge der verstorbenen Sängerin für insgesamt wohl rund 1,4 Millionen Pfund. Der Vater verklagte die beiden – und unterlag.

spiegel.title: Polen: Unbekanntes Flugobjekt dringt in Luftraum ein und stürzt ab
spiegel.description: Russland überzieht die Ukraine mit neuen Luftschlägen, auch nahe der polnischen Grenze. Dort geht kurze Zeit später der Alarm los, ein unbekanntes Objekt schlägt ein. Polens Regierungschef Tusk geht von einer Rakete aus.

elpais.title: Máxima alerta en Ceuta tras el cruce descontrolado de miles de personas desde Marruecos
elpais.description: La Guardia Civil y los medios de emergencia, superados, solo se ocupan de los heridos

elpais.title: Las imágenes de la llegada masiva de inmigrantes a la frontera de Ceuta con Marruecos: a nado y saltando las vallas
elpais.description: Entre la oleada de personas que ha cruzado a territorio de España y ha superado los medios de la Guardia Civil hay niños, jóvenes y familias

elpais.title: Marlaska viajará a Ceuta por la crisis de llegadas masivas a la frontera
elpais.description: El Gobierno de la ciudad autónoma había pedido al Gobierno la “emergencia nacional” y “mando único”, pero la normativa no incluye los flujos migratorios

elpais.title: Policías y guardias civiles alertan del colapso operativo en Ceuta por la entrada masiva de migrantes a nado: “Estamos desbordados”
elpais.description: Sindicatos y asociaciones de agentes creen la situación más grave que la de mayo de 2021, cuando entraron también miles de inmigrantes: “Aquella duró dos días y ahora llevamos una semana y no tiene pinta de que vaya a parar”

elpais.title: Cronología | La pinza entre la presión de Marruecos y de Vox en la intermitente crisis migratoria en Ceuta
elpais.description: “Soy muy del PP, pero el ministro hizo lo que yo le pedí”, declaró el popular Vivas ante el aluvión de llegadas en 2021

elpais.title: La Comunidad de Madrid anuncia que vende el ático de lujo de Chamberí el día después de revelarse su compra
elpais.description: El Gobierno de Ayuso alega que lo hace para “ayudar a la reconstrucción” por los incendios en la Sierra Oeste, después de las críticas por la noticia de EL PAÍS

elpais.title: Última hora de los incendios forestales, en directo | Sánchez anuncia el fin de la emergencia nacional en Ávila y Madrid
elpais.description: El incendio de Zamora arrasa 11.000 hectáreas en un día y obliga a desalojar 14 poblaciones | En León hay dos focos graves en Veguellina y Valdelaloba

elpais.title: Diario de un bombero (parte II): “La gran victoria ha sido la protección de la vida, que no haya muertos”
elpais.description: El efectivo Israel Naveso cuenta su “inmensa satisfacción de ser partícipe” de la estabilización de los incendios de Madrid y Ávila

elpais.title: Sara Aagesen: “Es el momento de que el PP aclare si se suma al negacionismo de la extrema derecha o a un pacto”
elpais.description: La vicepresidenta tercera y ministra para la Transición Ecológica critica que los populares “no sean capaces de sentarse con el Gobierno para un acuerdo frente a la emergencia climática”

elpais.title: Mil vecinos vuelven a casa mientras 7.000 siguen evacuados por el incendio de La Vall d’Uixó
elpais.description: Las llamas siguen fuera de control tras arrasar 9.644 hectáreas y devorar parte del parque natural de la Sierra de Espadán

elpais.title: Detenidos dos hombres de 51 y 42 años como presuntos responsables del incendio de Almorox
elpais.description: La investigación apunta a una negligencia al realizar actividades prohibidas con un riesgo extremo de incendios

elpais.title: John Healey, escritor hispanista: “Cuando murió Franco a los jóvenes nos entusiasmaba la democracia. Ahora es más difícil hablar libremente”
elpais.description: En 1969 vino a pasar una temporada en la finca del hijo díscolo y bohemio de un millonario importador de vinos estadounidense. España ya nunca salió de él: su autobiografía es una historia ‘sui generis’ de la España progresista

elpais.title: El lento declive de La Sexta
elpais.description: Es difícil saber si la causa para erosionar la imagen progresista de toda la cadena es la veleidad de los espectadores o aquel diálogo de Ferreras con Villarejo en el que aceptaba dar una información “muy burda”

elpais.title: Una octogenaria no puede cobrar un premio de la ONCE porque su marido la inscribió sin permiso en el registro de autoprohibición del juego
elpais.description: La mujer lucha en los tribunales para que se declare nula la inscripción realizada en 2012 por el hombre, ya fallecido

elpais.title: Los críticos se ríen de la obra artística de Adrien Brody: perros con bandana, pollo frito y un mural a lo Warhol
elpais.description: El actor neoyorquino lleva dos años centrado en la creación de grandes ‘collages’. En las subastas se venden por miles de dólares, pero para las redes y la crítica especializada siguen siendo motivo de burla

elpais.title: La extraña reinvención de Drea de Matteo, de Los Soprano: OnlyFans y el movimiento ultra son su segunda vida
elpais.description: Ganó un Emmy y fue una de las actrices más queridas de la televisión. Dos décadas después, la neoyorquina vende contenido en la plataforma para adultos, presenta un ‘podcast’ con figuras de la derecha alternativa y asegura que Hollywood la castigó por su negativa a vacunarse

elpais.title: Begoña Gómez recupera el pasaporte tras retirárselo el juez Peinado
elpais.description: El magistrado autorizó finalmente que otra persona recogiera la documentación en su nombre, según fuentes cercanas a la esposa del presidente del Gobierno

elpais.title: El juez Calama rechaza suspender la inspección de Hacienda a Zapatero y su familia
elpais.description: El magistrado descarta la petición de la Agencia Tributaria, que solicitó paralizar las investigaciones al expresidente mientras durara la instrucción de la Audiencia

nyt.title: Markets Challenge Warsh’s Approach to Taming Inflation
nyt.description: Kevin M. Warsh has made controlling inflation the top priority of his tenure as Federal Reserve chairman. But his hesitancy to embrace the possibility of higher borrowing costs has sparked a backlash.

nyt.title: U.S. Economic Growth Slowed in the Second Quarter
nyt.description: Gross domestic product expanded at a 1.5 percent annual rate over the past three months, as war in the Middle East shook energy prices and supply chains.

nyt.title: Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Eased During Pause in Iran War
nyt.description: Price pressures eased during a brief reprieve in the war with Iran, but the resumption of fighting suggests that inflation risks are still prevalent.

nyt.title: A ‘Credibility Shock’ Looms Over the Fed
nyt.description: Bonds sold off sharply after the Federal Reserve’s latest rate decision, signaling growing turmoil between the markets and the central bank.

nyt.title: How the War With Iran Is Widening, and U.S. Hospitals See a Surge of Uninsured Patients
nyt.description: Plus, the horrendous smell plaguing one Canadian town.

nyt.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Again, as Trump Encounters a More Determined Adversary in Widened War
nyt.description: The United States is again exchanging strikes with Iran, just days after the president appeared to reject plans to escalate.

nyt.title: U.S.-Saudi Attack on Iraqi Militias Risks Drawing Them into War
nyt.description: Iran-aligned militias in Iraq were under growing pressure to disarm, but the latest strikes may embolden them to get more deeply involved in the war.

nyt.title: Families Face Anxiety, Angst as Loved Ones Are Deployed to Fight Iran
nyt.description: As the war with Iran has continued, some are finding that the stress is bringing back old anxieties.

nyt.title: After Obamacare Cuts, Hospitals Are Treating More Uninsured Patients
nyt.description: More people who lost coverage after congressional Republicans ended enhanced federal subsidies are now seeking care in emergency rooms and unable to pay bills.

nyt.title: Bipartisan Anger Grows at Pentagon’s Delayed ‘Forever Chemicals’ Cleanups
nyt.description: Hundreds of bases are contaminated with PFAS, which are linked to low birth weight and other risks. Politicians from both parties are demanding explanations.

nyt.title: Poland’s Leader Says Russian Missile May Have Struck Its Territory During Ukraine Attack
nyt.description: Russian missiles have briefly entered Polish airspace in the past. Investigators have yet to definitively identify the object that struck Poland overnight.

nyt.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine With Missiles and Drones, Killing at Least 8
nyt.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said that a family of five had been killed at home in the latest in a series of large-scale aerial assaults by Moscow.

nyt.title: As China’s A.I. Gets Stronger, It Poses New Risks to Beijing
nyt.description: China’s A.I. rise is creating a new dilemma for Beijing. The open models that win influence abroad may pose risks to the country’s security and geopolitical strategy.

nyt.title: A.I. Data Centers in Space? A System to Cool Chips Could Help.
nyt.description: Researchers at Caltech and Sophia Space, a start-up, have developed a technology using solar power to prevent computer equipment from overheating in orbit.

nyt.title: China Threatens Retaliation as U.S. Moves to Block Robot Imports
nyt.description: The dispute highlights how robotics has become the latest battleground in the intensifying technological and industrial rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

nyt.title: Wildfires in Greece Kill 3 Firefighters as Blazes Still Burn in France and Spain
nyt.description: Greece also worked to contain blazes on Lesbos and in the Peloponnese, where another firefighter died, in the midst of a brutal wildfire season for Europe.

nyt.title: As Wildfires Plague Europe, Scotland Races to Save a Cherished National Park
nyt.description: As Europe’s climate warms, even moorlands and forests in the Cairngorms, in the Scottish Highlands, have fallen victim to rapidly spreading flames.

nyt.title: European Wildfires Amplified by Emptying Countryside and Fewer Farms
nyt.description: A warming planet and a shift away from farming have set the stage for larger fires on the continent. “We must learn to coexist with them,” one report said.

npr.title: Sen. Paul threatens to hold Fauci in contempt. And, a new rule undercuts U.S. asylum
npr.description: Sen. Rand Paul is moving to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he invoked his Fifth Amendment rights. And, the Trump administration has announced a new rule for the asylum process.

npr.title: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill at least 8 civilians and wound dozens
npr.description: The blitz expanded Russia's almost daily bombardment of Ukrainian cities as Moscow apparently looked to exploit Kyiv's critical shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defenses.

npr.title: The U.S. retaliates against a 'surprise attack' by Iran in Jordan
npr.description: The U.S. attacks were in retaliation for what the U.S. Central Command called "an attempted surprise attack" with ballistic missiles on Tuesday against U.S. forces in the Middle East.

npr.title: Hope dwindles for rescue in southwestern Japan quake as death toll climbs to 25
npr.description: Time was running out to find survivors, as rescuers continued to work in the Kumamoto area on Japan 's southern main island of Kyushu, where the magnitude 7.1 earthquake hit Tuesday.

npr.title: The race is on for the next United Nations secretary general
npr.description: The United Nations Security Council will begin straw polls Thursday to whittle down the field of candidates for the next U.N. secretary-general. Seven candidates are running to replace António Guterres.

npr.title: Latest Mideast strikes between U.S. and Iran draw Saudi Arabia into conflict
npr.description: The U.S. and Saudi Arabia struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq after they launched attacks.

npr.title: 'Taiwan Travelogue' rethinks history, colonialism, and identity
npr.description: The author and translator of Taiwan Travelogue, the winner of the 2026 International Booker Prize, discuss identity and history amid the debate over Taiwan's colonial ties to Japan and escalating geopolitical pressure from China.

npr.title: Greetings from an isolated region in northern Pakistan's Hindu Kush mountains
npr.description: Chitral borders Afghanistan and isn't easy to reach. Breathtaking views abound in this remote mountainous region — as do rockslides and avalanches.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran resume attacks. And, Fauci to face Senate questions on COVID pandemic
npr.description: The U.S. and Iran have resumed fighting after Iran attacked U.S. forces in the Middle East yesterday. And, a Senate committee will question Anthony Fauci about the COVID-19 pandemic.

npr.title: Iran resumes missile attacks as U.S. and Saudis strike Tehran-backed militias in Iraq
npr.description: The flare-up on multiple fronts raised the risk of a return to all-out war, underscoring the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has jolted the world economy.

republika.title: La guerra mondiale a pezzi comincia a saldarsi
republika.description: Le guerre non si fermano, ma questa newsletter prende una pausa di riposo e riflessione. Tornerà il 27 agosto

republika.title: Chat Delmastro, la mossa del cavallo di Lo Voi che ha mandato in tilt la maggioranza
republika.description: La lettera inviata dal procuratore di Roma ha costretto la Camera a fermarsi e rinviare il voto sull'utilizzabilità delle conversazioni tra l’ex sottosegretario alla Giustizia e Mario Caroccia

republika.title: Garanzia, pezzi di ricambio e modulo da compilare: come funziona il diritto alla riparazione Ue
republika.description: L’Italia non si adeguerà entro il 31 luglio alla normativa, che renderà più facile trovare i pezzi di ricambio e avere preventivi più chiari e trasparenti. In attesa della legge di recepimento, tutte le novità in arrivo

republika.title: Elettrodomestici e smartphone, cambia tutto: dall’Europa arriva il diritto alla riparazione
republika.description: I produttori devono intervenire sui beni tecnicamente recuperabili, con ricambi e manuali accessibili anche ai laboratori indipendenti. L’obiettivo è ridurre sprechi, rifiuti e costi per le famiglie, contrastando l’obsolescenza programmata

republika.title: I salari sono fermi al 1990 ma c'è la campagna elettorale. E il governo Meloni fa finta di niente
republika.description: Tagli alle tasse e all'Irpef, dicono premier e ministri. Ma secondo gli studi non basta a invertire la tendenza

republika.title: Siccità, binari deformati e fiumi quasi asciutti: così il caldo affonda i trasporti europei
republika.description: In Inghilterra il terreno argilloso si ritira, modifica la conformazione della strada ferrata rallentando i treni. Problemi anche a Londra lungo la Elizabeth line. Sul Reno in Germania le chiatte viaggiano con appena un decimo del carico normale: i prezzi per ogni tonnellata spostata vanno alle stelle

republika.title: Mattarella su Roggero: “Non si adatti legge al singolo. Tensioni elettorali non trascurino problemi"
republika.description: Il capo dello Stato alla cerimonia del Ventaglio al Quirinale: “La violenza è un virus letale per la democrazia”

republika.title: Inciampo alla Camera sul riconoscimento facciale. Richiamo da Bruxelles: “È vietato”
republika.description: Palazzo Chigi: rispetteremo l'AI Act. Madia (Italia viva): “Rinvio fatto gravissimo”

republika.title: Capoccia: “Oggi il vero pericolo per le democrazie sono le oligarchie della comunicazione”
republika.description: Intervista al professore ordinario di Politica comparata all’Università di Oxford. “I proprietari delle piattaforme, che gesticono gli algoritmi, hanno un potere senza precedenti. Gli Usa sono un caso, ma restano una democrazia liberale”

republika.title: No Tav, il prefetto vieta il campeggio a Susa e Bussoleno: controlli ai varchi verso il presidio
republika.description: Dopo gli scontri di Chiomonte, la polizia presidia gli accessi al nuovo campeggio vicino al cantiere di Susa e identifica i partecipanti. Proseguono le indagini sull'assalto di sabato, mentre il Viminale annuncia il massimo livello di vigilanza

republika.title: Alagna: “L’obiettivo di Mosca è mettere in crisi l’establishment democratico”
republika.description: Intervista all’esperto di integrità della comunicazione e minacce ibride, già advisor dell’Europarlamento, da anni studia le interferenze ordinate dal Cremlino. “Ora tentano anche di manipolare i dati di addestramento dell’IA”.

republika.title: Da Roberto Mancini alle “Case da vip”: così Facile Ristrutturare ha costruito il suo impero mediatico
republika.description: L’azienda aveva costruito la propria immagine grazie a testimonial famosi e social. Dietro la vetrina, però, si accumulavano debiti per 180 milioni di euro: ora i fondatori sono finiti in carcere con le accuse di bancarotta fraudolenta e autoriciclaggio

republika.title: Mondiali scherma, il Dream Team del fioretto è d’oro: Errigo avvia la rimonta sugli Usa
republika.description: A Hong Kong le azzurre travolgono le americane che erano in vantaggio di 4 stoccate, e si prendono la rivincita della finale delle Olimpiadi di Parigi. Quarto oro per l’Italia prima nel medagliere in uno dei Mondiali più ricchi di sempre

republika.title: Istat, Pil cresce oltre le attese: +0,2% nel trimestre. Meloni: “Continuate pure a sottovalutarci”
republika.description: Su base annua crescita dell’1%. Variazione acquisita dello 0,8%. Il ministro Giorgetti fa eco alla premier: “L’economia migliora nonostante il contesto negativo”

republika.title: Caldo estremo, arriva la quarta ondata: oggi 3, domani 11 città da bollino rosso
republika.description: Il Ministero della Salute amplia le aree interessate dal livello massimo di rischio. In Piemonte la maturazione delle uve accelera, mentre sul Gargano torna la minaccia dei roghi. Il Mediterraneo resta una delle zone più esposte agli effetti della crisi climatica

republika.title: Ferrari Luce sold out: in due mesi venduta la quota prevista per tutto il 2026
republika.description: Prenotate 500 auto elettriche, numero che il Cavallino aveva immaginato di mettere sul mercato fino a dicembre. Alla Cina piace il modello che fa discutere per il design. Ricavi e utili in crescita, stime riviste al rialzo e in Borsa il titolo sale del 2,9%

republika.title: Democrazia, Tomini: “Con il premierato di Meloni rischio deriva alla Trump e Orbán”
republika.description: Intervista al docente dell’Université libre de Bruxelles e ricercatore sulle autocratizzazioni e sulle forme di resistenza istituzionale e sociale

republika.title: Stellantis, il motore Nord America traina la ripresa. L’Europa fa più fatica. Giù il titolo
republika.description: Ricavi più 13% e utile torna positivo. La ripresa industriale e finanziaria del costruttore italo-francese tiene grazie soprattutto alle performance in Messico e Usa. Filosa: “Target 2026 confermati”.

phys-org.description: Bose–Einstein condensates are states of matter that form when particles called bosons are cooled to temperatures that are only a fraction of a degree above absolute zero (i.e., 0 Kelvin [-460°F]). phys-org.description: Nanoplastics—plastic particles smaller than one micrometer—are generated through the degradation and abrasion of plastic products and are increasingly detected in food, drinking water, air and biological tissues. phys-org.title: The role of community energy in mediating the sustainable energy transition
phys-org.description: Community energy projects, actively governed and managed by community members, play an essential role in advancing just energy transitions, for example, by providing energy in remote areas, facilitating the adoption of renewable technologies and building resilient electricity networks. proj-syn.title: Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

proj-syn.title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
proj-syn.description: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.

proj-syn.title: America Is Betting Against International Law
proj-syn.description: After cooperating with the International Criminal Court to indict Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes, the US has shifted to waging a scorched-earth campaign against the ICC in the name of protecting Israel. But rather than halting international law’s progress, the US is merely handing the pen to other countries.

proj-syn.title: The Therapist in Your Pocket
proj-syn.description: A new survey conducted by AXA and Ipsos shows that people are readily turning to AI chatbots to cope with mental-health problems. To ensure that these tools do more good than harm, health leaders, employers, insurers, and AI developers must take responsibility for steering them in a beneficial direction.

proj-syn.title: The Cost of Not Building Data Centers
proj-syn.description: In July, New York became the first state to enact a moratorium on new data centers, a path that other states may follow. But US policymakers, drawing lessons from past failures to make economy-wide investments in electrification and rare-earth processing, should weigh the strategic costs of not building essential infrastructure.

proj-syn.title: The Dangerous Spread of Jim Crow Nostalgia
proj-syn.description: With inaccurate claims about Black Americans’ poverty and crime rates having migrated from the far-right fringe to mainstream outlets like the Wall Street Journal, it is worth considering what the data actually say. Doing so will show that there is no empirical basis for such claims, only an ideological one.

proj-syn.title: The Gulf’s Push for AI-Led Governance
proj-syn.description: Governments around the world have spent decades outsourcing their ability to think to expensive consultants, gradually ceding the knowledge and judgment needed to govern effectively. AI may now offer a way to reverse that trend, and Gulf countries are providing an early glimpse of what that may look like.

proj-syn.title: India’s Exam Worriers Become Democracy Warriors
proj-syn.description: Generations of students in India have resigned themselves to the idea that the education system is primarily a sorting mechanism, which rewards compliance. But as recent protests showed, the system's rigidity, together with insufficient rewards in the form of good jobs, has rendered this approach untenable.

proj-syn.title: Why Business Leaders Are Souring on AI
proj-syn.description: Companies have poured billions of dollars into AI in anticipation of transformative productivity gains and cost savings, but the returns have yet to justify those investments. Rising costs, intellectual-property risks, and mounting cybersecurity threats call for a more disciplined approach to AI adoption.
